title: Working up tunes from records at rehearsal
summary: The band took tunes off records, spending a few hours at rehearsal, and played them before rival bands to make hits.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Work along with him. I see. And we used to clean up on that. How long, if you were starting on a new tune like that, taking it off a record or something,
how long on the average would it take you to work up a piece? A day?
We'd be at it one or two hours and couldn't get it. I see. And we'd bring it up for the next rehearsal, I guess.
But after four or five hours, you generally have it put together?
Yeah, we have it put together.
And when you played that piece as the years went by, would you always play it approximately the same way that you worked it out?

Same. Same way that come off the record. I see. But now you would be, many times, see, we was very good on getting that, as far as it was very good, you see? Uh-huh. And we would get out and play those things before the other fellas would get them, you see? Oh, I see. And you'd make your hits, you see? Because they'd hear them on records, you see, or sit down and listen down and stuff, and they did their dancing. And when it came out, we'd be playing it. Well, then we would be playing it.
